claim_verdicts.evidence: servers/index.md: "[Kestrel server] is the default, cross-platform HTTP server implementation." kestrel.md L19: "Kestrel is the recommended server for ASP.NET Core, and it's configured by default in ASP.NET Core project templates." Dropping the templates clause in round 3 does not weaken the claim; "default" is the docs' own word. Only uncontradicted caveat: under IIS in-process hosting the server is IIS HTTP Server, which this lesson never mentions.

servers/index.md L17: "An ASP.NET Core app runs with an in-process HTTP server implementation. The server implementation listens for HTTP requests and surfaces them to the app as a set of request features composed into an HttpContext." kestrel/options.md shows the server itself doing the byte work (RequestHeadersTimeout: "maximum amount of time the server spends receiving request headers"; MaxRequestHeaderFieldSize). The lesson's TCP/HTTP-1.1 scoping matches defaults: http3.md L60 "HTTP/3 isn't enabled by default."
claim_verdicts.source: refs/aspnetcore-docs: servers/index.md L17; servers/kestrel/options.md L84,L114; servers/kestrel/http3.md L60

claim_verdicts.evidence: servers/index.md L17 has the server only surfacing requests as features on HttpContext - no mention of meaning or dispatch. routing.md L20: "Routing is responsible for matching incoming HTTP requests and dispatching those requests to the app's executable endpoints. Endpoints are the app's units of executable request-handling code. Endpoints are defined in the app and configured when the app starts." Route choice and logic are app middleware, not the server.

kestrel/when-to-use-a-reverse-proxy.md: "When Kestrel is configured to listen on a port, Kestrel handles all traffic for that port regardless of requests' Host headers." The spreading work is listed as the proxy's, not Kestrel's: "A reverse proxy: ... Simplifies load balancing and secure communication (HTTPS) configuration." servers/index.md L17: "An ASP.NET Core app runs with an in-process HTTP server implementation." The round-3 rewording (no "load balancer") stays inside this evidence.

servers/index.md L17: the server "listens for HTTP requests and surfaces them to the app as a set of request features composed into an HttpContext" - accepting is not the whole job. kestrel/options.md documents that parsing work as the server's own: RequestHeadersTimeout "gets or sets the maximum amount of time the server spends receiving request headers", MaxRequestHeaderFieldSize, and "The default maximum request body size is 30,000,000 bytes".

issues.quote: Caddy runs your C# code the same way it sends back a file from disk.
issues.text: Deleting the Try it aside removed claim 10, but the file-from-disk assertion survives here and in quiz q1 option c ("the same way Caddy sends back a file from disk"), so a specific, checkable statement about Caddy now sits outside the ledger. The statement is true at the tag: Caddyfile L11 "root * /srv/www", L87-89 "handle { file_server }", docker-compose.yml mounts ./www:/srv/www:ro, and www/index.html, cached.html, login.html exist at stage-0. No lesson text needs changing.
issues.fix: Re-add one claim to .meta.json (section 6, kind fact, no version_key): "At stage-0 Caddy serves static files from disk (root * /srv/www plus file_server in the fallback handle block)", source_hint "examples/don-hang@stage-0: Caddyfile L11, L87-89; www/index.html". Leave the misconception bullet and quiz q1 option c as written.

issues.quote: Caddy runs your C# code the same way it sends back a file from disk.
issues.text: Nothing in the lesson shows Caddy returning a file from disk. The only Caddy behaviour I was shown is a `respond` line with a literal string in `Caddyfile`. So this comparison explains nothing to me and I had to skip it, unsure whether serving files is a third Caddy behaviour I missed somewhere.
issues.fix: In the third "Beginners often think…" bullet, delete the comparison so the claim reads: **"Caddy runs your C# code for you."** Leave the "Actually…" correction sentence unchanged.

issues.quote: Reads a fixed file and returns it, the same way Caddy sends back a file from disk
issues.text: Same unexplained behaviour as the section 6 bullet. Worse, explanation c tells me this "describes a web server like Caddy in this course so far" and that Kestrel differs by not "returning a fixed file". Section 5 showed Caddy returning a fixed string, never a file, so the explanation left me less sure what Caddy does. I still answered a.
issues.fix: In q1, change option c to "Returns a fixed string typed into a config file, the way Caddy answers at stage-0", and in explanation c replace "returning a fixed file" with "returning a fixed string".

issues.quote: parsing them into well-formed HTTP (start line, headers, body)
issues.text: The lesson and the prerequisite both call this part the "first line". "start line" appears only here, and I stopped to work out whether it is the same part under another name or a further part I was never taught.
issues.fix: In q5 explanation "correct", replace "start line" with "first line" (en) and "start line" with "dòng đầu" (vi).

issues.quote: distributing across machines is a separate concern placed in front of it, not something Kestrel does
issues.text: This, and "another piece in front of it" in q5 explanation d, assume something can stand in front of Kestrel. The lesson never mentions anything in front of Kestrel, so I cannot picture what that is and I suspected I had missed a paragraph.
issues.fix: Remove the spatial phrase in both places: q1 explanation b → "…distributing work across machines is a separate job, not something Kestrel does"; q5 explanation d → "…nothing in the lesson says a web server needs a second program to work".

issues.quote: This matters when a real handler already exists and the team is choosing among HTTP methods
issues.text: "handler" is a word I have not met. The lesson uses `handle @postOrder` as the name of a Caddy block and, separately, "a C# method". I cannot tell which of the two a "handler" is.
issues.fix: In q6 explanation d, replace "a real handler already exists" with "real C# code already answers that path" (and the matching vi wording).

issues.quote: Decides which SQL query to run against the database for this request
issues.text: "SQL query" is a term neither this lesson nor my earlier lessons gave me; I know tables, rows, joins and transactions, not this word. It did not block me — the lesson says plainly that Kestrel decides nothing about what a request means — but I was reading a word I do not own.
issues.fix: In q1 option d and explanation d, replace "which SQL query to run against the database" with "what to read from or write to the database".

issues.quote: every POST there today gets the same fixed JSON back from Caddy, the web server running the lab, whose whole behaviour is written in one text file, `Caddyfile`.
issues.text: I read this sentence twice. It chains the goal, today's behaviour, Caddy and `Caddyfile` in one line, and by "whose whole behaviour" I had lost whether "whose" points at Caddy or at the lab.
issues.fix: Split it in two: "…gets the same fixed JSON back from Caddy, the web server running the lab. Caddy's whole behaviour is written in one text file, `Caddyfile`."
